clue.text: Charm south-east Italian leader

parts.note: Il Duce was the title taken by Mussolini

explanation.surface: A tourist is beguiled by a leader from Italy's south-eastern regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a noun but works here as a verb; DUCE is Italian for leader, Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile or win someone over with attraction is to entice or lure them, a close verbal synonym.

clue.text: Nervous about bottom of chair getting damaged

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, the one kept

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious that the base of a chair is getting broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarred bears marks of injury, so it has been damaged.

clue.text: Spaniards concealing revolting sewer

indicators.note: revolting is read as turning over, so the letters run backwards
a word concealing something holds it within its letters

parts.note: the run of letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Spanish people are covering up a disgusting sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' seems to describe the sewer, but it tells you to read the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a channel or pipe that carries away waste water, as a sewer does.

clue.text: Brightest climbers initially left mountain

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The best climbers set off first and left the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright here means intelligent, so the most clever people are the brightest.

clue.text: Naive painting reduced

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A painting dismissed as unsophisticated and cut down in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without guile or sophistication is innocent and simple, which is what naive describes.

clue.text: A time to coax and go

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to tempt is to coax or entice

explanation.surface: A moment for persuading someone to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like a verb of leaving, but here it is a noun: have a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is a try or turn at something, the same as an attempt.

clue.text: Measures items exploding

indicators.note: exploding blows something apart, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes readings as objects blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: To time something is to clock or gauge its duration, so a verb meaning measures fits.

clue.text: Explain delight about posh police department

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to account for their glee over an upmarket police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: U is an old label for upper-class usage; CID is the British police's detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make something clear by clarifying it, a formal synonym for explain.

clue.text: Discovered leaders of some universities suggested students employed deception

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each following word is kept

parts.words: some universities suggested students employed deception
parts.note: the opening letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Academic heads found out that students had been cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: To suss something out is informal British for working it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sussed a thing means having worked it out or found the truth, so it was discovered.

clue.text: One picking nits from pet and dancing

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: Someone grooms the lice off a pet, then dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking nits' suggests grooming an animal; here it is nitpicking, fussing over tiny errors.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over trivial details and petty mistakes, which is what a nitpicker does.

clue.text: Degradation in a cellar

explanation.surface: Something rots and decays down in an underground storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as A plus a word for an underground room.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliation that lowers a person's dignity or standing is degradation, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Savages low quality housing rejected across area

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
lying across something means stretching around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a slum is squalid, poor housing
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Poor housing is turned down across a whole district, and its people are treated savagely.
explanation.definitionFit: To maul is to attack and tear viciously, as a wild animal does, which is what savages means as a verb.

clue.text: Called end to intense row

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: Someone shouted to stop a heated argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a line of things, such as a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of hills or products is a line or series of them, just as a row is.

clue.text: Give weapons to cities involved in ceasefire

parts.note: to arm is to supply weapons

indicators.note: involved means tangled or convoluted, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A call to supply weapons to towns caught up in a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement between warring sides to stop fighting, a truce.

clue.text: Detective inspectors dispatched to protest

parts.note: DI is the abbreviation for detective inspector, plural DIS

explanation.surface: Police officers are sent out to deal with a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protest' reads as a noun for a demonstration; the answer also works as a verb meaning to object.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree openly with an official view is to object or demur, so the verb protest fits.

clue.text: One bent on retaliation after son caught person going through the bins

indicators.note: after places the second idea behind the first ones in the finished word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A vengeful figure stalks a son caught rifling through dustbins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who searches through rubbish for usable things is a scavenger.

clue.text: Couple noisily joining jailbird

indicators.note: noisily means the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a couple is two; its sound is written another way
the can is slang for prison
a single printed word that the setter splits in two: its first half is wordplay and its second half is the definition

explanation.surface: A noisy pair team up with a convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jailbird' reads as one word, but it splits: jail gives the letters and bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A toucan is a tropical bird with an enormous brightly coloured beak.

clue.text: Lower job stress

parts.note: a line of work is a job

explanation.surface: A less senior post brings pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' looks like a noun for strain, but it is a verb: to emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise it, the verbal sense of stress.

clue.text: Congress initially take steps to get American plant

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: to act is to take steps or take action

explanation.surface: Congress moves quickly to obtain an American factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests an industrial plant beside Congress; here it is a living one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny succulent that grows in deserts, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Little bit of broth's available we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the sound of the phrase is what counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a cry that the broth is ready to serve

explanation.surface: A rumour that only a little soup is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The French borrowing is usually written with a cedilla, soupçon.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a very small amount or trace of something, a tiny bit.

clue.text: Deity dodges around the centre of Bristol

indicators.note: around suggests being moved about, so the letters are rearranged
the centre of a word is its middle letter, here the one kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter Bristol

explanation.surface: A god sidesteps its way around the middle of Bristol, a city in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: A goddess is a female divine being worshipped in a religion or mythology, one kind of god.

clue.text: Drive Ford model right into another vehicle

parts.note: to go is to drive or travel
the Ka is a small Ford car
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A driver steers a Ford straight into another car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' makes sense because the Ford in the wordplay is already a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-kart is a small low open racing car, a different kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Wrong cherries regularly open

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Faulty cherries keep splitting open.
explanation.definitionFit: An open, frank person is honest and genuine, which is what sincere means.

clue.text: Young creatures left in grottos

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Baby animals are abandoned in caverns.
explanation.definitionFit: Calves are the young of cattle, whales and elephants, so they are young creatures.

clue.text: Ace you and I hit is impressed

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
you and I together are we
struck is the past tense of strike, hit

explanation.surface: A brilliant shot the two of us played has impressed onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being filled with awe or wonder means being deeply moved and amazed, so impressed fits.

clue.text: Touch part of heating element

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone touches a component of an electric heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a slight trace, as in a touch of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or hint of something, as is a touch.

clue.text: Steal popular bird

explanation.surface: A thief takes a much-loved bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small songbird with a red breast, common in British gardens.

clue.text: Head of studio wearing footwear to provide elevation

indicators.note: wearing something means having it on the outside, so it wraps the piece
the head of a word is its first letter, the one kept

explanation.surface: A film studio boss wears platform shoes to look taller.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost is to lift or raise something up, so it gives elevation.

clue.text: Woman rejecting animal products, say, found in vehicle

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A woman who shuns meat and dairy turns up travelling in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a verb but stands for EG, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats and uses nothing derived from animals; the clue's woman is one such person.

clue.text: Rambling vicar on about one craving flesh

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so these letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: A vicar drones on in a rambling sermon about lust of the flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnivore is an animal that eats meat, so it hungers for flesh.

clue.text: Offspring hiding desire for doctor

indicators.note: to hide something is to hold it inside, so one word wraps around another

explanation.surface: A child conceals a longing to see a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, a kind of doctor.

clue.text: British support returning the French bug

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: British backing coming back to France over a computer glitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is an informal word for an insect, and a beetle is one kind of insect.
